groups.title: File-Based Routing
groups.question: You are building a Remix app with a dashboard layout, project pages and settings pages. Explain how file names become routes and how nesting works.

followUps.Route File Naming Conventions: How do dots and underscores in route file names work?
followUps.Nested Routes and Outlet: What happens if a parent route forgets to render Outlet?

evidence.text: Dots in file names become slashes in the URL.
A $ prefix marks a dynamic segment.
A leading underscore creates a layout route that does not add to the URL.
Nested routes map URL parts to nested components.
The parent renders an Outlet where the child route appears.
Without it, child routes do not show up at all.

groups.title: Navigation and Links
groups.question: Your navigation sometimes reloads the whole page and you need to redirect after a successful action. Explain Remix's navigation tools.

followUps.Link vs NavLink and Prefetching: What do Link and NavLink add over a plain anchor, and how does prefetching work?
followUps.useNavigate and Programmatic Navigation: When should you use useNavigate, and where is a redirect better?

evidence.text: Link navigates without a full reload.
NavLink also knows whether it is the active route, for styling.
Prefetch options load route data early, such as on hover.

notEnough: Only saying Link is for navigation.

evidence.text: useNavigate navigates from code in event handlers or effects.
It should not be called during render.
After actions, returning a redirect from the server is usually better.

groups.title: Route Params and Search
groups.question: Your user page reads an id from the URL and the search page keeps filters in the query string. Explain how you would read and update route data safely.

followUps.Dynamic Segments and useParams: How do you read a dynamic segment, and why validate it?
followUps.useSearchParams for Query Strings: How does useSearchParams handle query strings?

evidence.text: A $userId segment captures that part of the URL.
It is available as params in loaders and through useParams in components.
It is user input, so it must be validated before querying the database.

notEnough: Only saying params come from the URL.

evidence.text: useSearchParams reads the current query parameters.
Its setter updates them and triggers a navigation.
Changing window.location directly bypasses Remix and reloads the page.

notEnough: Only saying it reads the query string.

groups.title: Remix App Structure
groups.question: After a refactor, no client-side JavaScript works in your Remix app, and enabling all future flags at once broke several pages. Explain the app shell and configuration.

followUps.root.tsx and App Shell: What does root.tsx render, and why does removing Scripts break interactivity?
followUps.remix.config.js and vite.config.ts: How should you adopt future flags?

evidence.text: root.tsx renders the HTML document shell for every page.
The Scripts component loads the client JavaScript.
Without it, pages render but nothing on the client works.

notEnough: Only saying root.tsx is the root.

evidence.text: The Vite config controls adapters, route settings and future flags.
Future flags should be enabled one at a time.
Testing after each one makes breakage easy to trace.

notEnough: Only saying you change the config.
